data_source.name: NJ CRC: Cannabis Sales Totals (quarterly, 'Rec Med Sales Q2 26' PDF)
data_source.notes: The CRC publishes sales quarterly, not monthly, so 'monthly' is empty and figures are in 'quarterly'. 'adult_use' = recreational sales, 'medical' = medicinal sales. The CRC notes some figures are updated after a prior quarter's report; values here are from the Q2 2026 edition. Annual figures are the CRC's own TOTALS rows.

tax_note: Adult-use cannabis is subject to New Jersey's 6.625% sales tax, a Social Equity Excise Fee on cultivator transfers, and a municipal transfer tax of up to 2% where adopted (NJ Division of Taxation).
summary: New Jersey's adult-use market opened in April 2022 and passed $1 billion in annual recreational sales in 2024. Recreational sales reached $1.12 billion in 2025, up about 12% on 2024, and the CRC reported $270.1 million in the second quarter of 2026. Medical sales have collapsed, from $226 million in 2022 to $46 million in 2025, as patients buy at adult-use counters instead. More licensed stores keep opening, but recreational sales in the first half of 2026 were only about 1% above the same period of 2025. The CRC publishes only quarterly totals.

faq.q: How much cannabis does New Jersey sell?
faq.a: Recreational sales were $270.1 million in the second quarter of 2026 and $1.12 billion in 2025, according to the Cannabis Regulatory Commission.

faq.q: Does New Jersey publish monthly cannabis sales?
faq.a: No. The CRC publishes quarterly sales totals for recreational and medicinal cannabis.

faq.q: What happened to New Jersey's medical cannabis sales?
faq.a: They fell from $226.1 million in 2022 to $46.2 million in 2025 as patients shifted to the adult-use market.
